## Global Warming (Adapted from Problem 7.19 in OpenIntro, 4th Edition)

To determine whether there is evidence of a rise in global temperatures, we are going to examine temperature differences in 1948 vs 2018. 197 locations from the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration's (NOAA) historical data were sampled; these locations have data available for both 1948 and 2018. We want to determine if there were more days with temperatures exceeding 90 degrees Fahrenheit in 1948 or 2018. The difference in number of days exceeding 90 degrees Fahrenheit (number of days in 2018 - number of days in 1948) was calculated for each of the 197 locations. The average if these differences was 2.9 days with a standard deviation of 17.2 days. We are interested in determining whether these data provide strong evidence that there is a difference in the number of days in 2018 that exceeded 90 degrees Fahrenheit vs 1948 from NOAA's weather stations. 

The data for these 197 locations are loaded with the openintro package; the name of the data set is climate70.

To do a paired test, we need to calculate the difference between number of days in 2018 above 90 degrees and the number of days in 1948 above 90 degrees and create a new column in our data set. The following code will create that new column:

```{r}
climate70$dx90_diff <- climate70$dx90_2018 - climate70$dx90_1948
```
